title: Dragon Ball Super Artist Returns With New Look at Original Villain Amid Hiatus
content:
The Dragon Ball Super manga has been on hiatus ever since Akira Toriyama’s death in March 2024. Written by Toriyama and illustrated by Toyotaro, the manga was released in 2015 as a sequel to the original story. Dragon Ball originally concluded its serialization in 1995, which is why its return two decades later was the most exciting surprise for fans. Thanks to the franchise’s global impact, it maintained a huge fan base even two decades after the main story’s ending. The sequel manga follows Goku and the others in a new set of adventures that take place after the Buu Saga, where Kid Buu was defeated. However, the manga has been on hiatus for more than two years, and fans are still waiting for Toyotaro to take over the helm.

While the manga hasn’t shared any updates on its return, artist Toyotaro continues his special project titled “Toyotaro Drew This.” The project began in December 2017 to share monthly visuals of Dragon Ball characters who did not have a lot of screen time in the story. Over the years, Toyotaro has shared over 90 illustrations of forgotten or underrated characters, including Captain Ginyu, Bardock, Raditz, Gregory, and many more. These visuals are always shared on the official website of Dragon Ball , where you can also keep up with all the updates from the franchise.

Dragon Ball Super Artist Returns With a New Look At Guarana

The latest October 2026 visual shares a new look at Guarana, an underrated villain from Dragon Ball Super. He is the second most powerful member of Frieza’s army led by Sorbet. The character first appeared in the Battle of Gods arc, where Frieza was planning to take revenge on the Saiyans. He also discovered the Super Dragon Balls, but just when he was about to report it to headquarters, Champa witnessed his actions and destroyed his spaceship along with him. There was never a chance that the character would survive an attack from a God of Destruction who was out to kill him. Guarana stood out for his unique character design rather than his role in the story or his powers.

Dragon Ball Super Needs to Return With a New Saga

In February last year, Toyotaro released a single chapter before continuing the hiatus. While the manga’s return date hasn’t been revealed yet, the official X handle of V Jump described it as a “serializing” work, confirming that Toyotaro will be returning with new chapters. The official account also recently reposted Toyotaro , who assured fans that he will return with the manga. The artist has big shoes to fill after Toriyama’s death, which is all the more reason a long break was necessary. However, after these latest updates, likely that Dragon Ball Super ‘s return is sooner than expected.

The extra chapter released last year concluded the Super Hero Saga, so we can expect the manga to return with a brand new story. This also means a new adventure for Goku and the Z Fighters, so anything could happen after the series resumes its monthly serialization. With no release window or first look at the manga’s return so far, it’s impossible to determine how the story will proceed from here on out. At the very least, we know that Goku and the Z Fighters will continue to face more powerful opponents as the story continues. The latest Saga of the series expands on the story of the 2022 film, Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero , centering around Piccolo and Gohan. This is all the more reason another arc with Goku at the center is needed as soon as the manga’s return.

title: After 30 Years, Legendary Action Series to Return for New Spinoff Ahead of Anime Reboot
content:
It’s only been a month since the anime reboot of Eat-Man was confirmed, and now it already has a streaming home. Via a press release, Crunchyroll confirmed acquiring streaming rights to the anime when it premieres. While the release date and other details haven’t been revealed yet, fans can expect new updates in a few weeks or months. The reboot, titled Eat-Man: The Over Order , was announced last month, more than 30 years since the manga debut. The 1990s were a revolutionary era for the Shonen demographic since many of them etched their names in history. Eat-Man is one of those stories that was initially popular thanks to its exceptional story but didn’t stand the test of time.

Rather than being a blockbuster hit, Eat-Man was more of a cult classic , especially in Japan. Written and illustrated by Akihito Yoshitomi, the manga even released an anime adaptation in 1997, but it didn’t adapt the entire story. Yoshitomi is known for classics such as School Ningyo, Blue Drop , and more. Three decades after leaving this thrilling story incomplete, Studio Cab confirmed a reboot adaptation. Thanks to Crunchyroll bringing the anime to international regions, the series is finally getting the hype it deserves.

What Is the New Eat-Man Spin-Off About?

So far, the plot and premise of the manga haven’t been revealed yet, but we can expect more details after its debut in the Monthly Shonen Sirius magazine by Kodansha. The official X handle of EAT-MAN The Over Order, the new anime project for Akihito Yoshitomi’s Eat-Man manga, announced this week that Yoshitomi will launch a spinoff manga adaptation of the upcoming anime, titled Desert-Dessert. The manga will be released in the January 2027 issue of Kodansha’s Monthly Shonen Sirius magazine on November 26th, 2026. However, while the manga has already shared the title and date, there hasn’t been any confirmation regarding the international release.

We might have to wait until the release to check if it will be available on the online manga platform of Kodansha, K Manga. While K Manga has made it easier than ever for global fans to read more manga series, it doesn’t have all of Kodansha’s titles. Additionally, after a few months of serialization, the manga will begin releasing its volumes, so we can count on official English translations as well. Since it’s a monthly series, these updates will take at least a year or even longer.

What Do We Know About Eat-Man Reboot?

Since the reboot was announced only a month ago , a final trailer or even a release window hasn’t been revealed yet. Fans only got a first look in the visual that features Bolt, the central character. This sci-fi action centers around a mysterious adventurer named Bolt Crank who devours metal and regenerates any weapon. His past is shrouded in mystery, while his true purpose also remains hidden from those around him. Bolt takes on requests and travels across the world, where he gets entangled in countless incidents and fateful encounters along the way. The story is episodic in nature as it focuses on self-contained vignettes and short stories rather than a single linear plot. It follows Bolt throughout his journey as he keeps arriving in new locations while dealing with personal struggles and conflicts. He also helps those he encounters before moving on to a different location.

title: Sanrio's Kuromi Character Gets 1st Film in 2027
content:
Sanrio announced on Saturday that its Kuromi character will star in her first film, which the distributor GAGA open in Japan next year. The company made the announcement with an English-subtitled video message from Kuromi on Halloween, which is also Kuromi's birthday.

The film's website location indicates that the film will have the title "Kuromi the Movie." The website and the video message's description say that "release information for territories outside Japan will be announced once confirmed."

Kuromi made her debut not in Sanrio 's own character goods line, but in the television anime Onegai My Melody in April 2005. She gradually became a popular character in her own right, and spawned two series of Kuromi's Pretty Journey anime shorts in 2023 and 2024, as well as a stop-motion anime My Melody & Kuromi on Netflix in July 2025.

title: Crunchyroll’s Darkest Fall 2026 Anime Celebrates Halloween With Creator’s Spooky Tribute
content:
Crunchyroll ‘s darkest Fall 2026 anime continues to emerge as one of the spookiest series of the season, and its creator is embracing the same vibe with a special tribute to celebrate Halloween. The end of October brings an exciting and spooky atmosphere, adding a different kind of energy. Not every holiday is as unique as Halloween, and for fans of the anime, it certainly wouldn’t be complete without a series that perfectly captures its spirit. Fans have been blessed with arguably one of the spookiest anime in recent years this season, which also happens to be a heavy action series. The Vermilion Mask , currently airing and animated by 100studio, has been hitting it out of the park with its dark elements.

Based on the manga of the same name by Nabana Naba, the series follows a dark and tragic narrative as its protagonist embarks on a journey to destroy the masks and prevent another tragedy from occurring. As the anime continues to air and delve deeper into its story with twists and turns, the creator has shared a special illustration of the main character celebrating Halloween. It features the protagonist, Peru , sitting on a classic Halloween pumpkin as he wishes fans a Happy Halloween.

Crunchyroll’s The Vermilion Mask Celebrates Halloween With a Perfect Illustration

The illustration features Peru sitting on the pumpkin, making a peace sign and saying “trick or treat,” while the pumpkin, with its spooky expression, glows from within. The illustration clearly highlights Peru’s friendly nature, while the pumpkin seems to have something different in mind, suggesting that Peru won’t let it trick anyone else. This creates a playful dynamic between the two. On a deeper level, the illustration also perfectly symbolizes what this anime is about. Peru is on a journey to destroy the mischievous masks that could cause the same tragedy he experienced during his childhood. He is doing everything he can while keeping his kindness intact and ensuring that no one else gets hurt in the process.

This is also why Peru doesn’t want anyone else to become part of his journey, as he plans to stop the madness caused by the masks all alone. The Vermilion Mask isn’t just a dark anime featuring tragic characters ; it is also fun and spooky, with all these elements coming together to highlight its unique appeal. With Peru sporting different types of masks that grant him various abilities, such as the Spider Mask giving him spider-like abilities and the Chameleon Mask allowing him to camouflage himself, even the action elements of the series are fun and intriguing.

Now, another character, Mok, has appeared, bringing his own mask-related condition, and his presence further amplifies the spooky vibe with his smoke abilities. With only three episodes released so far, The Vermilion Mask is the perfect new anime currently airing this fall season. It is emerging as a modern seinen anime that balances fun elements with twists that keep viewers on the edge of their seats . As the anime continues airing throughout the season, The Vermilion Mask will keep delivering Halloween’s spooky vibes with new episodes every Saturday on Crunchyroll.

title: 3 Coolest Great Ape Transformations in Dragon Ball History
content:
Super Saiyan wasn’t the first transformation in Dragon Ball history, as it all started when Goku became the Great Ape Oozaru in the original series. No one knew that Saiyans had a connection to apes or what the tail represented at first , and there was no way Goku could know as he would unconsciously do it when he looked at the moon. This transformation became the official start of his and everyone else’s journey in learning more about Saiyans.

However, the look continued to progress. Initially, it fell by the wayside once Super Saiyans were introduced. The power up just looked so cool, but Akira Toriyama did an incredible job of always advancing the levels that fighters in the Dragon Ball universe would attain so it rarely returned. Furthermore, a power level never lost its luster either. Toriyama and the anime team found a way to reincorporate old looks into the Great Ape form and reinvent them as well.

3) Cumber’s Super-Saiyan-Inspired Transformation

This one definitely got the audience. It had been quite some time since the Great Ape had appeared on screen, and it was only referenced in flashbacks prior to Cumber’s transformation. The Evil Saiyan was introduced as a masked madman in Super Dragon Ball Heroes . He didn’t ever go Super Saiyan in the first battle he appeared in. However, he gave Goku and Vegeta all they could handle when he took on the Great Ape form.

The significance of his change was that he maintained a lot of his human accoutrements. He kept his mask, clothes and broken restraints on. Cumber also saw his hair change into a similar look to a Super Saiyan 3 Golden Great Ape hybrid. The look was so unique that it had to make the list, despite it not being canon.

2) Goku Debuts Great Ape In First Series

The opening curveball of the series had to come when Goku tapped into his Saiyan heritage and became the Great Ape for the first time. Dragon Ball was much more a kids show and didn’t have quite the violent, high-stakes nature of the ensuing shows. This goofy kid with a tail has only really showed a fun-loving side for the most part. But in one moment of looking at the moon, he grows large fangs, changes his eyes to red and becomes a towering, violent ape.

The first time Oozaru appeared on screen it just gave a different feel to the show and where it might be headed. Although it was a gradual climb into what the show is now. Toriyama really clued everyone into what could be coming down the line, and it was a tremendous reveal.

1) Goku Becomes First Golden Great Ape

Even if it’s not canon and the transformation wasn’t around for a long time after, Goku turning into the Golden Great Ape before eventually going Super Saiyan 4 is peak Dragon Ball nostalgia. On the heels of Dragon Ball Z’s events, the creators of the show woke everyone from their long lapse without the Great Ape. Since the last significant time the audience had seen the ape, Super Saiyan and all its grades, Super Saiyan 2, Super Saiyan 3 and fused Saiyans had all made an appearance.

It felt like that the Great Ape form was almost not needed, as it was far less powerful. But this wasn’t the case at all as this off-speed pitch caught everyone off guard. Goku looked at the Earth this time to transform which had never happened before. He then transforms into a Super Saiyan-Oozaru hybrid that Baby Vegeta was not expecting. Then, to pull a second changeup and turn him into a Super Saiyan 4 was such a great payoff. This whole saga is probably the peak of Dragon Ball GT ‘s run.

It was able to introduce new levels of power against a villain that felt insurmountable . Baby wasn’t the final villain of the show but to introduce the return of the Great Ape here at this moment in the story proved perfect. Do you think the list got it right? Let us know in the comments.

title: This Gundam Anime Had the Coolest Redesigns in the Anime’s Toonami History
content:
American audiences got to experience Mobile Suit Gundam Wing in early 2000 when it made its debut with Toonami, and in less than a year, the show’s popularity continued to rise with the abbreviated series Mobile Suit Gundam Wing: Endless Waltz . The three-episode release was comparable to a sequel film , but the artwork felt lightyears ahead. The detail on the Gundam suits was cleaned up, and most noticeably numerous suits received significant facelifts.

This made quite a difference for the United States fanbase in particular. Although the movie was a video release, it made the original TV series look like a massive upgrade in a short amount of time. Whereas plenty of other anime were looking pretty dated up to that point. Endless Waltz felt much more futuristic and ahead of its time, and that was cemented with its redesigns.

Mobile Suits Went Platinum In Endless Waltz

The addition of actual wings on Wing Gundam Zero, dual double gatling guns and a darker paint scheme on Heavyarms and Tallgeese III’s overpowering, hulking rebuild are just a few of the major changes to the mobile suits. Yes, the improved animation and CGI immediately made the newest Gundam Wing edition better, but the complete overhaul of most of the mobile suits put the anime over the top. Most of the suits just doubled down on their pilots’ styles and personalities, but it hammered the points home.

Tallgeese III’s newest look matched Zechs Merquise’s anonymous style to perfection. The hidden visor on the head crest with no expression and the dominance of the scale just fit his mysterious background. Heavyarms Gundam was already a machine gun monstrosity, and this edition just adds more edgy style to Trowa Barton. The circus clown and Gundam pilot’s serious demeanor mixed so well with the darkened paint scheme and chaotic combat style.

Duo Maxwell’s Deathscythe got its own dark upgrade changing to Gundam Deathscythe Hell edition. This one featured the famous cape/bat wings look. The wings envelop the Gundam and become a wearable shield that fits the tone of the suit. They can then branch out, and look like a bat’s wings. Duo Maxwell calling himself the God of Death in the original series just tied a bow on this slick pairing between man and machinery. The main Gundam in the series weren’t the only suits to get an awesome upgrade either.

Forget the bland Leo foot soldier suits from the series, the Serpent flipped the script from scrawny battlefield into mini Heavyarms. These suits are not Gundam, but they received added armor and double-barreled gatling guns just like the Heavyarms. Which was a nice added detail to the series that proved it wasn’t just the Gundam tearing through simple mobile suits. They enemies responded to the technological upgrades in kind with upgrades of their own.

Raises Potential For Even More Upgraded Suits

Gundam is always creating and modifying the current suits in their catalogue . This series will likely be no different, even though it went dormant years ago. Endless Waltz made major aesthetic updates, but it also lacked screen time to truly make an impact on the wider franchise. The three episodes brought a close to the series 30 years ago in Japan.

There was a teaser that the series could return with the anime adaptation of Frozen Teardrop someday. In that manga, the suits received even more suit alterations and it would be great to see them on screen next. Bandai has an opportunity to bring back the show and jump on the nostalgia train, but right now, nothing else has been confirmed. Do you think Endless Waltz had the best redesigns and should the series return soon? Let us know in the comments.

contentBlocks.text: American audiences got to experience Mobile Suit Gundam Wing in early 2000 when it made its debut with Toonami, and in less than a year, the show’s popularity continued to rise with the abbreviated series Mobile Suit Gundam Wing: Endless Waltz . The three-episode release was comparable to a sequel film , but the artwork felt lightyears ahead. The detail on the Gundam suits was cleaned up, and most noticeably numerous suits received significant facelifts.

This made quite a difference for the United States fanbase in particular. Although the movie was a video release, it made the original TV series look like a massive upgrade in a short amount of time. Whereas plenty of other anime were looking pretty dated up to that point. Endless Waltz felt much more futuristic and ahead of its time, and that was cemented with its redesigns.
Mobile Suits Went Platinum In Endless Waltz

contentBlocks.credit: Image Courtesy of Bandai Namco Filmworks

contentBlocks.text: The addition of actual wings on Wing Gundam Zero, dual double gatling guns and a darker paint scheme on Heavyarms and Tallgeese III’s overpowering, hulking rebuild are just a few of the major changes to the mobile suits. Yes, the improved animation and CGI immediately made the newest Gundam Wing edition better, but the complete overhaul of most of the mobile suits put the anime over the top. Most of the suits just doubled down on their pilots’ styles and personalities, but it hammered the points home.

Tallgeese III’s newest look matched Zechs Merquise’s anonymous style to perfection. The hidden visor on the head crest with no expression and the dominance of the scale just fit his mysterious background. Heavyarms Gundam was already a machine gun monstrosity, and this edition just adds more edgy style to Trowa Barton. The circus clown and Gundam pilot’s serious demeanor mixed so well with the darkened paint scheme and chaotic combat style.

Duo Maxwell’s Deathscythe got its own dark upgrade changing to Gundam Deathscythe Hell edition. This one featured the famous cape/bat wings look. The wings envelop the Gundam and become a wearable shield that fits the tone of the suit. They can then branch out, and look like a bat’s wings. Duo Maxwell calling himself the God of Death in the original series just tied a bow on this slick pairing between man and machinery. The main Gundam in the series weren’t the only suits to get an awesome upgrade either.

Forget the bland Leo foot soldier suits from the series, the Serpent flipped the script from scrawny battlefield into mini Heavyarms. These suits are not Gundam, but they received added armor and double-barreled gatling guns just like the Heavyarms. Which was a nice added detail to the series that proved it wasn’t just the Gundam tearing through simple mobile suits. They enemies responded to the technological upgrades in kind with upgrades of their own.
Raises Potential For Even More Upgraded Suits

contentBlocks.credit: Image Courtesy of Bandai Namco Filmworks

contentBlocks.text: Gundam is always creating and modifying the current suits in their catalogue . This series will likely be no different, even though it went dormant years ago. Endless Waltz made major aesthetic updates, but it also lacked screen time to truly make an impact on the wider franchise. The three episodes brought a close to the series 30 years ago in Japan.

There was a teaser that the series could return with the anime adaptation of Frozen Teardrop someday. In that manga, the suits received even more suit alterations and it would be great to see them on screen next. Bandai has an opportunity to bring back the show and jump on the nostalgia train, but right now, nothing else has been confirmed. Do you think Endless Waltz had the best redesigns and should the series return soon? Let us know in the comments.

title: Brazil's CCXP Screens World Premiere of Garena Free Fire Game's Free Fire Daybreak Anime
content:
Kadokawa and Garena Online Private Limited announced on Friday that they will screen the world premiere of the first episode of Free Fire Daybreak , the television anime adaptation of Singaporean game developer and publisher Garena 's Garena Free Fire battle royale shooting game, at this year's CCXP event in São Paulo, Brazil on December 5. There will also be a panel featuring the anime's production team and DJ and producer Alok.

CCXP26 will take place from December 3-6 at São Paulo Expo.

The companies describe the story:

In the near-future city of New Dawn, ruled by the powerful Horizon Corporation, 16-year-old Kelly becomes entangled in the experimental "Project Bloom" and awakens “Limit Break”, an extraordinary ability capable of unlocking anything that has been sealed away. As fragments of her past begin to resurface, Kelly joins newfound allies to uncover the conspiracy surrounding Horizon Corporation and confront the forces threatening the future of New Dawn. What fate lies ahead?

Ken Takahashi ( Ragna Crimson , Fate/kaleid liner Prisma Illya ) is directing the anime. Japanese studio Candy Box ( Blue Archive The Animation , Azur Lane: Slow Ahead! ) is producing the anime. Sus4 Inc. ( Ragna Crimson ) is producing the music.

The anime is planned to be broadcast and streamed worldwide. Kadokawa and Garena are co-producing the anime. Kadokawa 's Kadokawa Qingyu subsidiary is the production manager.

Garena Free Fire is a third-person shooter game. Like other games in the battle royale genre, players are dropped into a large island alongside dozens of other players, collecting supplies and weapons as they go. The objective of the game is to be the last person standing, varying strategies between actively hunting down other players, or attempting to hide as other players eliminate each other.

Garena debuted Garena Free Fire in December 2017. Sensor Tower's data.ai website puts the game as the world's most downloaded mobile game from 2019 to 2021, and the most downloaded mobile battle royale in 2022 and 2023. The game had 100 million daily active users in February 2024.

title: After 27 Years, Boruto Just Destroyed Naruto’s Most Important Element
content:
The Naruto series first appeared in Shonen Jump magazine in September 1999, and its very first chapter made it clear what its most important element would be. Now, the latest installment in the franchise, Boruto: Two Blue Vortex , has just destroyed the representation of this element and what it means for the franchise. The Boruto series has been quite different, despite embodying many elements of the Naruto franchise. It had to make several elements of the original series obsolete as it focused on a new generation and brought about revolutionary changes. It began doing so with the incorporation of scientific elements, showcasing the world’s advancement and the changing role of ninjas.

Then came the original series’ main characters, who were either made irrelevant or, like Naruto and Sasuke, sidelined by certain circumstances. All of this was done to allow the next generation to take the spotlight. However, one element the series continued to incorporate was its political dynamic, in which the position of Hokage always played a central role. For the most part, Naruto served as Hokage and fulfilled his duties admirably. Following his entrapment, Shikamaru took over and also fulfilled his duties as Hokage. However, the latest chapter of Boruto: Two Blue Vortex appears poised to replace Shikamaru as Hokage, but it is not simply aiming to introduce a new Hokage; rather, it is changing what the position itself stands for.

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Disrespects the Most Important Element of the Naruto Franchise

When the Naruto series first appeared, it made it clear that its titular protagonist’s journey would be about becoming Hokage, which meant earning everyone’s respect and being recognized as a person. This is what drove Naruto throughout the series, and he ultimately achieved his dream and became the honorable Hokage he had always wanted to be. However, the Boruto series has failed to preserve this meaning, and ever since Shikamaru became Hokage, it has been sidelining the position. Now, with the appearance of Kobu, the representative of the Fire Nation’s Daimyo, the position of Hokage has been further undermined. Kobu has repeatedly questioned Shikamaru and his authority as Hokage.

In the latest chapter of Boruto: Two Blue Vortex , Chapter 38 , Kobu reveals that he has obtained evidence against Shikamaru and can replace him with Konohamaru. While Konohamaru is a suitable choice, as he has always aspired to become Hokage himself, Kobu’s plan is simply to fill the position while pulling the strings himself. This dishonors the position of Hokage, which has always represented the pride of Konoha and its shinobi. To make matters worse, Kobu and other high-ranking political figures are planning to dismiss the shinobi forces entirely, as they no longer consider them useful in the modern era. This marks a major shift, with undermining the position of Hokage being one of the first steps.

The Naruto franchise has indeed evolved considerably, especially in its portrayal of the position of Hokage , which is ultimately a political office. When Naruto became Hokage and began carrying out his duties, he realized what his dream was actually about. At the end of the day, the Hokage was a political figure, and the position’s exploitation through corruption was somewhat inevitable. The Boruto series has done well to reflect the realities of the elements established by the Naruto franchise. While its reasoning for undermining the position of Hokage is genuine, it is still sad to see the role being stripped of the meaning it held for Naruto in the original series.

title: Hiragi-san's House of Vampires Manga Gets TV Anime
content:
A new official website opened on Saturday to announce that Miki Yoshikawa 's Hiragi-san's House of Vampires ( Hiiragi-san no Kyūketsu Jijō ) manga is inspiring a television anime adaptation by UNLIMITED PRODUCE by TMS . The website unveiled a visual:

Kodansha 's K MANGA service is publishing the manga in English, and it describes the story:

Every family has its own “secrets”... Meet our protagonist, Shota Minamoto, a junior-high student who also happens to be an orphan in a children's home. One day, he was adopted by a family living in a luxurious, Japanese-style estate. Welcomed warmly by them all, Shota started letting his guard down, but this family had a “secret” that the world could never know. A new work from the creator of “The Cuckoo's Fiance” showcasing a different kind of “family.” Thus begins a cozy, bloody love comedy!

Yoshikawa ( A Couple of Cuckoos ) debuted the manga in Kodansha 's Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine in October 2021. Kodansha published the manga's sixth compiled book volume in November 2025. Yoshikawa published a one-shot for the "family comedy" manga in 2019.
